#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""ecfix.py - minimal EditorConfig enforcement tool.

Parses .editorconfig files (own minimal parser), matches files against
section globs with fnmatch (later sections override earlier ones), and
checks files for violations.

Supported properties:
    indent_style, indent_size, end_of_line,
    insert_final_newline, trim_trailing_whitespace

Usage:
    python3 ecfix.py [--fix] ROOT PATH [PATH ...]

Without --fix: report violations, exit 1 if any found.
With --fix:    apply ONLY safe mechanical corrections:
                 * trim trailing whitespace
                 * add missing final newline
                 * CRLF -> LF conversion
               (indentation problems are reported but never auto-fixed)
"""

import argparse
import fnmatch
import sys
from pathlib import Path

SUPPORTED_KEYS = {
    "indent_style",
    "indent_size",
    "end_of_line",
    "insert_final_newline",
    "trim_trailing_whitespace",
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parsing

def parse_editorconfig(path):
    """Parse a .editorconfig file.

    Returns a list of (glob_pattern, props_dict) in file order.
    Later entries override earlier ones when matching a file.
    """
    sections = []
    current_glob = None  # top-level (e.g. "root = true") -> ignored
    for raw in Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";"):
            continue
        if line.startswith("[") and line.endswith("]"):
            current_glob = line[1:-1].strip()
            if not any(g == current_glob for g, _ in sections):
                sections.append((current_glob, {}))
            continue
        if "=" in line and current_glob is not None:
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            key = key.strip().lower()
            value = value.strip()
            if key in SUPPORTED_KEYS:
                sections[-1][1][key] = value
    return sections


def props_for(relpath, sections):
    """Merge properties of every glob section matching relpath.

    Later sections override earlier ones, mirroring EditorConfig's
    "last match wins" rule.
    """
    merged = {}
    posix = relpath.replace("\\", "/")
    base = posix.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    for pattern, props in sections:
        # Patterns containing '/' are anchored to the .editorconfig dir;
        # bare globs match the basename at any depth.
        if "/" in pattern:
            matched = fnmatch.fnmatch(posix, pattern.lstrip("/"))
        else:
            matched = fnmatch.fnmatch(base, pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(posix, pattern)
        if matched:
            merged.update(props)
    return merged


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- checking

def _iter_lines(data):
    return data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").split("\n")


def check_file(data, props):
    """Return list of human-readable violations for file bytes."""
    issues = []
    text = data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    lines = text.split("\n")

    has_crlf = "\r\n" in text
    has_bare_lf = data.replace(b"\r\n", b"").find(b"\n") != -1

    eol = props.get("end_of_line")
    if eol == "lf" and has_crlf:
        issues.append("end_of_line: CRLF line endings found (expected LF)")
    elif eol == "crlf" and has_bare_lf:
        issues.append("end_of_line: bare LF line endings found (expected CRLF)")

    if props.get("trim_trailing_whitespace", "").lower() == "true":
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if ln.rstrip("\r").rstrip() != ln.rstrip("\r"):
                issues.append(f"line {i}: trailing whitespace")
                break

    if props.get("insert_final_newline", "").lower() == "true":
        if data and not data.endswith(b"\n"):
            issues.append("missing final newline")

    indent_style = props.get("indent_style", "").lower()
    if indent_style == "tab":
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
            body = ln.rstrip("\r")
            if body.startswith(" ") and body.strip():
                issues.append(f"line {i}: space indentation (indent_style=tab)")
                break
    elif indent_style == "space":
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
            body = ln.rstrip("\r")
            if body.startswith("\t") and body.strip():
                issues.append(f"line {i}: tab indentation (indent_style=space)")
                break

    indent_size = props.get("indent_size", "")
    if indent_size.isdigit() and int(indent_size) > 0 and \
            indent_style == "space":
        size = int(indent_size)
        for i, ln in enumerate(lines, 1):
            body = ln.rstrip("\r")
            stripped = body.lstrip(" ")
            n = len(body) - len(stripped)
            if n and stripped and n % size != 0:
                issues.append(
                    f"line {i}: indent of {n} spaces is not a "
                    f"multiple of indent_size={size}")
                break

    return issues


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fixing

def fix_file(data):
    """Apply ONLY: trailing-whitespace trim, final newline, CRLF->LF."""
    data = data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")

    out = []
    for ln in data.split(b"\n"):
        out.append(ln.rstrip(b" \t"))
    data = b"\n".join(out)

    if data and not data.endswith(b"\n"):
        data += b"\n"
    return data


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- driver

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="EditorConfig enforcement tool")
    ap.add_argument("--fix", action="store_true",
                    help="apply safe corrections (whitespace/newline/CRLF)")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default=".editorconfig",
                    help="path to .editorconfig (default: <ROOT>/.editorconfig)")
    ap.add_argument("root", help="project root holding .editorconfig")
    ap.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="files to check (relative to root)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    root = Path(args.root)
    cfg = root / args.config if not Path(args.config).is_absolute() else Path(args.config)
    sections = parse_editorconfig(cfg)

    total_bad = 0
    fixed = 0
    for name in args.paths:
        fpath = root / name
        if not fpath.is_file():
            print(f"{name}: MISSING FILE", file=sys.stderr)
            total_bad += 1
            continue
        data = fpath.read_bytes()
        props = props_for(name, sections)
        issues = check_file(data, props)
        if not issues:
            print(f"{name}: OK")
            continue
        total_bad += 1
        if args.fix:
            new_data = fix_file(data)
            remaining = check_file(new_data, props)
            fpath.write_bytes(new_data)
            fixed += 1
            if remaining:
                print(f"{name}: PARTIALLY FIXED, still violating:")
                for msg in remaining:
                    print(f"    - {msg}")
                total_bad += 1
            else:
                print(f"{name}: FIXED ({', '.join(issues)})")
        else:
            print(f"{name}: VIOLATIONS:")
            for msg in issues:
                print(f"    - {msg}")

    if args.fix:
        print(f"\n{fixed} file(s) rewritten.")
    else:
        verdict = "clean" if total_bad == 0 else f"{total_bad} file(s) with violations"
        print(f"\ncheck complete: {verdict}")
    return 1 if total_bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def fix_file(data):
    """Apply ONLY: trailing-whitespace trim, final newline, CRLF->LF."""
    data = data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")

    out = []
    for ln in data.split(b"\n"):
        out.append(ln.rstrip(b" \t"))
    data = b"\n".join(out)

    if data and not data.endswith(b"\n"):
        data += b"\n"
    return data


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- driver

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="EditorConfig enforcement tool")
    ap.add_argument("--fix", action="store_true",
                    help="apply safe corrections (whitespace/newline/CRLF)")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default=".editorconfig",
                    help="path to .editorconfig (default: <ROOT>/.editorconfig)")
    ap.add_argument("root", help="project root holding .editorconfig")
    ap.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", help="files to check (relative to root)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    root = Path(args.root)
    cfg = root / args.config if not Path(args.config).is_absolute() else Path(args.config)
    sections = parse_editorconfig(cfg)

    total_bad = 0
    fixed = 0
    for name in args.paths:
        fpath = root / name
        if not fpath.is_file():
            print(f"{name}: MISSING FILE", file=sys.stderr)
            total_bad += 1
            continue
        data = fpath.read_bytes()
        props = props_for(name, sections)
        issues = check_file(data, props)
        if not issues:
            print(f"{name}: OK")
            continue
        total_bad += 1
        if args.fix:
            new_data = fix_file(data)
            remaining = check_file(new_data, props)
            fpath.write_bytes(new_data)
            fixed += 1
            if remaining:
                print(f"{name}: PARTIALLY FIXED, still violating:")

                    print(f"    - {msg}")
                total_bad += 1
            else:
                print(f"{name}: FIXED ({', '.join(issues)})")
        else:
            print(f"{name}: VIOLATIONS:")
            for msg in issues:
                print(f"    - {msg}")

    if args.fix:
        print(f"\n{fixed} file(s) rewritten.")
    else:
        verdict = "clean" if total_bad == 0 else f"{total_bad} file(s) with violations"
        print(f"\ncheck complete: {verdict}")
    return 1 if total_bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Tests for ecfix.py — EditorConfig enforcement tool.

The full check -> fix -> re-check scenario is rebuilt from scratch in a
pytest tmp_path for every test, with byte-level assertions on the files
after fixing.
"""

import importlib.util
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ECFIX = HERE / "ecfix.py"

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ecfix", ECFIX)
ecfix = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(ecfix)


def run(root, *paths, fix=False):
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(ECFIX)]
    if fix:
        cmd.append("--fix")
    cmd += [str(root), *paths]
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)


EDITORCONFIG = """\
root = true

[*]
end_of_line = lf
insert_final_newline = true
trim_trailing_whitespace = true

[*.py]
indent_style = tab
indent_size = 4

[*.md]
indent_style = space
indent_size = 2
"""


def make_tree(root: Path):
    """Recreate the mini-tree used in the manual demo."""
    (root / ".editorconfig").write_text(EDITORCONFIG, encoding="utf-8")

    # .py: tab-indented per config, but trailing spaces + no final newline
    (root / "bad.py").write_bytes(
        b"def greet():\n"
        b"\tprint('hi')   \n"
        b"\treturn 'hi'\t"
    )
    # .md: CRLF endings + trailing whitespace + no final newline
    (root / "bad.md").write_bytes(
        b"# Title  \r\n"
        b"\r\n"
        b"Some text.\r\n"
        b"- item one\r\n"
        b"- item two\t\r\n"
    )
    # fully compliant file
    clean_bytes = b"x = 1\n"
    (root / "clean.py").write_bytes(clean_bytes)
    return clean_bytes


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tests


def test_check_mode_reports_violations_and_exit_1(tmp_path):
    make_tree(tmp_path)
    proc = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py")
    assert proc.returncode == 1
    assert "bad.py: VIOLATIONS:" in proc.stdout
    assert "trailing whitespace" in proc.stdout
    assert "missing final newline" in proc.stdout
    assert "CRLF line endings found" in proc.stdout
    assert "clean.py: OK" in proc.stdout
    assert "check complete: 2 file(s) with violations" in proc.stdout


def test_fix_then_recheck_full_scenario(tmp_path):
    """The exact demo workflow: check -> fix -> check, byte-verified."""
    clean_bytes = make_tree(tmp_path)

    # 1. initial check fails
    assert run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py").returncode == 1

    # 2. fix pass succeeds
    fixed_run = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py", fix=True)
    assert fixed_run.returncode == 0, fixed_run.stdout + fixed_run.stderr

    # byte-level assertions on what --fix actually wrote
    assert (tmp_path / "bad.py").read_bytes() == (
        b"def greet():\n"
        b"\tprint('hi')\n"
        b"\treturn 'hi'\n"
    )
    assert (tmp_path / "bad.md").read_bytes() == (
        b"# Title\n"
        b"\n"
        b"Some text.\n"
        b"- item one\n"
        b"- item two\n"
    )
    # untouched clean file must be byte-identical
    assert (tmp_path / "clean.py").read_bytes() == clean_bytes

    # 3. re-check is clean and exits 0
    recheck = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py")
    assert recheck.returncode == 0
    assert "bad.py: OK" in recheck.stdout
    assert "bad.md: OK" in recheck.stdout
    assert "check complete: clean" in recheck.stdout


def test_fix_is_idempotent(tmp_path):
    make_tree(tmp_path)
    run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", fix=True)
    after_first = {
        p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in tmp_path.iterdir() if p.is_file()
    }
    second = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", fix=True)
    assert second.returncode == 0
    for name, data in after_first.items():
        assert (tmp_path / name).read_bytes() == data


def test_indent_violations_detected_but_never_autofixed(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / ".editorconfig").write_text(
        "[*.py]\nindent_style = tab\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    spacey = b"def f():\n    return 1\n"
    (tmp_path / "spacey.py").write_bytes(spacey)

    check = run(tmp_path, "spacey.py")
    assert check.returncode == 1
    assert "space indentation" in check.stdout

    run(tmp_path, "spacey.py", fix=True)
    # --fix only touches whitespace/EOL/newline: indentation stays as-is
    assert (tmp_path / "spacey.py").read_bytes() == spacey


def test_later_sections_override_earlier(tmp_path):
    cfg = tmp_path / ".editorconfig"
    cfg.write_text("[*]\nend_of_line = lf\n[*.md]\nend_of_line = crlf\n",
                   encoding="utf-8")
    sections = ecfix.parse_editorconfig(cfg)
    assert ecfix.props_for("notes.md", sections)["end_of_line"] == "crlf"
    assert ecfix.props_for("script.py", sections)["end_of_line"] == "lf"


def test_glob_matching_with_fnmatch(tmp_path):
    cfg = tmp_path / ".editorconfig"
    cfg.write_text("[test_*.py]\ninsert_final_newline = false\n",
                   encoding="utf-8")
    sections = ecfix.parse_editorconfig(cfg)
    props = ecfix.props_for("src/pkg/test_app.py", sections)
    assert props["insert_final_newline"] == "false"
    assert ecfix.props_for("src/pkg/app.py", sections) == {}


def test_missing_final_newline_detection_unit(tmp_path):
    issues = ecfix.check_file(b"hello", {"insert_final_newline": "true"})
    assert any("final newline" in i for i in issues)
    assert ecfix.check_file(b"hello\n", {"insert_final_newline": "true"}) == []


def test_crlf_to_lf_fix_unit():
    assert ecfix.fix_file(b"a\r\nb\r\n") == b"a\nb\n"
    # bare CR is not part of the CRLF->LF correction

The full check -> fix -> re-check scenario is rebuilt from scratch in a
pytest tmp_path for every test, with byte-level assertions on the files
after fixing.
"""

import importlib.util
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ECFIX = HERE / "ecfix.py"

spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("ecfix", ECFIX)
ecfix = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(ecfix)


def run(root, *paths, fix=False):
    cmd = [sys.executable, str(ECFIX)]
    if fix:
        cmd.append("--fix")
    cmd += [str(root), *paths]
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)


EDITORCONFIG = """\
root = true

[*]
end_of_line = lf
insert_final_newline = true
trim_trailing_whitespace = true

[*.py]
indent_style = tab
indent_size = 4

[*.md]
indent_style = space
indent_size = 2
"""


def make_tree(root: Path):
    """Recreate the mini-tree used in the manual demo."""
    (root / ".editorconfig").write_text(EDITORCONFIG, encoding="utf-8")

    # .py: tab-indented per config, but trailing spaces + no final newline
    (root / "bad.py").write_bytes(
        b"def greet():\n"
        b"\tprint('hi')   \n"
        b"\treturn 'hi'\t"
    )
    # .md: CRLF endings + trailing whitespace + no final newline
    (root / "bad.md").write_bytes(
        b"# Title  \r\n"
        b"\r\n"
        b"Some text.\r\n"
        b"- item one\r\n"
        b"- item two\t\r\n"
    )
    # fully compliant file
    clean_bytes = b"x = 1\n"
    (root / "clean.py").write_bytes(clean_bytes)
    return clean_bytes


# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tests


def test_check_mode_reports_violations_and_exit_1(tmp_path):
    make_tree(tmp_path)
    proc = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py")
    assert proc.returncode == 1
    assert "bad.py: VIOLATIONS:" in proc.stdout
    assert "trailing whitespace" in proc.stdout
    assert "missing final newline" in proc.stdout
    assert "CRLF line endings found" in proc.stdout
    assert "clean.py: OK" in proc.stdout
    assert "check complete: 2 file(s) with violations" in proc.stdout


def test_fix_then_recheck_full_scenario(tmp_path):
    """The exact demo workflow: check -> fix -> check, byte-verified."""
    clean_bytes = make_tree(tmp_path)

    # 1. initial check fails
    assert run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py").returncode == 1

    # 2. fix pass succeeds
    fixed_run = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py", fix=True)
    assert fixed_run.returncode == 0, fixed_run.stdout + fixed_run.stderr

    # byte-level assertions on what --fix actually wrote
    assert (tmp_path / "bad.py").read_bytes() == (
        b"def greet():\n"
        b"\tprint('hi')\n"
        b"\treturn 'hi'\n"
    )
    assert (tmp_path / "bad.md").read_bytes() == (
        b"# Title\n"
        b"\n"
        b"Some text.\n"
        b"- item one\n"
        b"- item two\n"
    )
    # untouched clean file must be byte-identical
    assert (tmp_path / "clean.py").read_bytes() == clean_bytes

    # 3. re-check is clean and exits 0
    recheck = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", "clean.py")
    assert recheck.returncode == 0
    assert "bad.py: OK" in recheck.stdout
    assert "bad.md: OK" in recheck.stdout
    assert "check complete: clean" in recheck.stdout


def test_fix_is_idempotent(tmp_path):
    make_tree(tmp_path)
    run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", fix=True)
    after_first = {
        p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in tmp_path.iterdir() if p.is_file()
    }
    second = run(tmp_path, "bad.py", "bad.md", fix=True)
    assert second.returncode == 0
    for name, data in after_first.items():
        assert (tmp_path / name).read_bytes() == data


def test_indent_violations_detected_but_never_autofixed(tmp_path):
    (tmp_path / ".editorconfig").write_text(
        "[*.py]\nindent_style = tab\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    spacey = b"def f():\n    return 1\n"
    (tmp_path / "spacey.py").write_bytes(spacey)

    check = run(tmp_path, "spacey.py")
    assert check.returncode == 1
    assert "space indentation" in check.stdout

    run(tmp_path, "spacey.py", fix=True)
    # --fix only touches whitespace/EOL/newline: indentation stays as-is
    assert (tmp_path / "spacey.py").read_bytes() == spacey


def test_later_sections_override_earlier(tmp_path):
    cfg = tmp_path / ".editorconfig"
    cfg.write_text("[*]\nend_of_line = lf\n[*.md]\nend_of_line = crlf\n",
                   encoding="utf-8")
    sections = ecfix.parse_editorconfig(cfg)
    assert ecfix.props_for("notes.md", sections)["end_of_line"] == "crlf"
    assert ecfix.props_for("script.py", sections)["end_of_line"] == "lf"


def test_glob_matching_with_fnmatch(tmp_path):
    cfg = tmp_path / ".editorconfig"
    cfg.write_text("[test_*.py]\ninsert_final_newline = false\n",
                   encoding="utf-8")
    sections = ecfix.parse_editorconfig(cfg)
    props = ecfix.props_for("src/pkg/test_app.py", sections)
    assert props["insert_final_newline"] == "false"
    assert ecfix.props_for("src/pkg/app.py", sections) == {}


def test_missing_final_newline_detection_unit(tmp_path):
    issues = ecfix.check_file(b"hello", {"insert_final_newline": "true"})
    assert any("final newline" in i for i in issues)
    assert ecfix.check_file(b"hello\n", {"insert_final_newline": "true"}) == []


def test_crlf_to_lf_fix_unit():
    assert ecfix.fix_file(b"a\r\nb\r\n") == b"a\nb\n"
    # bare CR is not part of the CRLF->LF correction
    assert ecfix.fix_file(b"a\rb\n") == b"a\rb\n"

def test_each_violating_file_is_clean_after_fix(tmp_path, name):
    make_tree(tmp_path)
    assert run(tmp_path, name, fix=True).returncode == 0
    assert run(tmp_path, name).returncode == 0
